about: The regression gate `ai-classification` asks for: transaction -> expected account ->
expected treatment -> expected decision. Run it before shipping any change to the
prompt, the model, the rules, memory, or tax logic.
Three kinds of case, scored differently:
settled  — one right answer. Bank fees are bank fees.
policy   — more than one defensible answer; `alsoAccept` lists them. The GST
outcome is the same either way, so only the P&L line differs and the
firm decides. Scored as correct if any listed code is returned.
abstain  — the description cannot settle it. Coding it confidently is the
failure; routing it to a person is the pass.
The headline number is not accuracy. It is falseAutoApproval: coded with enough
confidence to skip review, and wrong. That is the one CLAUDE.md says the business
lives or dies on (<= 0.5%). A model that abstains too often only costs review time.
The `settled` expectations are ordinary bookkeeping, not tax advice. The registered
tax advisor should confirm them before this file is treated as authoritative.

cases.why: Principal to the loan repayments account (650, flagged for the advisor: typed as an expense in the supplied chart). The interest portion is split at acceptance from the loan schedule, not guessed here.

The supply of water is GST-free but a Sydney Water bill carries taxable service charges too, so the split decides the BAS figure. Account 360 is GST_ON_EXPENSES and 365 is GST_FREE_EXPENSES — picking either one blind puts a wrong number at 1B. The tax advisor sets the policy.
Also a TPAR-reportable payment: the subcontractor link is set at review.
Software or a subscription. Same GST either way.

$2,199 sits near the instant asset write-off threshold, which this system has no verified value for. Expensing it (340 Computer Equipment and Software, or 550 Tools and Equipment) or capitalising it is a tax decision, not a coding one.
